question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over the type I region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{1}{4}\le x\le \frac{1}{2},\,x\le y\le 1-x\}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{2y}{x}\,dA & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}{\int }_{x}^{1-x}\frac{2y}{x}\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}{\int }_{x}^{1-x}\frac{2y}{x}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{1}{x}[{\int }_{x}^{1-x}2y\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{1}{x}[{y}^{2}]_{x}^{1-x}dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{1}{x}((1-x)^{2}-{x}^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{1}{x}(1-2x)dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}(\frac{1}{x}-2)dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}(\frac{1}{x}-2)dx & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2x]_{1/4}^{1/2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2})-1-(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{4})-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$
